authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6914.1 nakha explicitly gives Palula nāṅg and regional nahu/nauh “fingernail”. Retained-k nok forms may require the separately numbered *nakkha or learned/regional nakha transmission, so are not assigned by an old unsplit link alone. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10702 rātrī gives Palula rōt, widespread rāt and the addendum’s Western Pahari rāc “night”. Thus the Kului affricate is directly supported in the neighboring primary comparison. Retroflex final ṭ remains a transcription/local-correspondence question. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2574 ka explicitly gives eastern ke “who”, Palula ko and Khowar ka, with what/why ka in the Western Pahari addendum. Survey what/where forms need to be separated from local kim-derived or adverbial constructions; the who forms are the immediate supported subset. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.
